weeks.title: Build a sentence
weeks.spanish: Identifica sujeto y verbo. Con he/she/it o un sujeto singular, agrega -s: the coordinator checks; my job needs it. Con I/you/we/they usa verbo base. Usa need to + verbo para una acción necesaria.

weeks.title: Now or usually?
weeks.spanish: Usa presente simple para hábitos; am/is/are + -ing para acciones en curso.

weeks.title: Tell the story
weeks.spanish: Usa pasado simple para acciones terminadas. Después de did usa verbo base; send cambia a sent. Usa the para algo identificado. Las frases son work on y wait for.

weeks.title: Connect your ideas
weeks.spanish: Relaciona ideas: because da una razón, so da un resultado y but introduce contraste.

weeks.title: Share an update
weeks.spanish: Da un avance, un bloqueo y un siguiente paso. Usa need to + verbo.

weeks.title: Plan what comes next
weeks.spanish: Will sirve para decisiones o predicciones; going to para planes. Present continuous también expresa acuerdos.

weeks.title: Make meetings useful
weeks.spanish: Después de do, does y did usa el verbo base. Pide aclaración con preguntas concretas.

weeks.title: Work through dependencies
weeks.spanish: Nombra la dependencia, explica su impacto y pide una acción con fecha.

weeks.title: Lead a conversation
weeks.spanish: Usa peticiones claras y corteses. Distingue un riesgo posible de un problema actual.

weeks.title: Negotiate a deadline
weeks.spanish: Explica la restricción y ofrece una alternativa viable. If + presente, will + verbo.

weeks.title: Tell your professional story
weeks.spanish: Organiza una respuesta con situación, acción y resultado. Usa ejemplos ficticios.

weeks.title: Bring it all together
weeks.spanish: Une pasado, presente y futuro. Resume lo esencial y confirma el siguiente paso.

rows: Introduce yourself
What do you do on Project Orion? I coordinate the design team.
The speaker coordinates a team.
I ___ the design team.
coordinate
She coordinate the design team.
She coordinates the design team.
Add -s to a present-simple verb after she, he, or it.
Name a responsibility
Who checks the weekly report? The project coordinator checks it every Friday.
The report is checked each Friday.
The coordinator ___ the report.
checks
He need a clear plan.
He needs a clear plan.
The coordinator is one person, so use checks with -s. The same agreement rule gives he needs, not he need. I, you, we, and they use the base form.
Ask about a role
Does the designer attend the planning meeting? Yes, she attends every Monday.
The designer attends a regular meeting.
___ the designer attend meetings?
Does
Does she attends meetings?
Does she attend meetings?
After does, use the base verb: attend.
Explain what you need
What do you need to start? We need to review the design first.
A design review must happen first.
We need ___ review the design.
to
We need review the design.
We need to review the design.
Use need to + base verb to describe a necessary action.
A simple introduction
Are you the project coordinator? Yes, I am. I work with two designers.
The speaker works with two designers.
I ___ the project coordinator.
am
I is responsible for planning.
I am responsible for planning.
Use am with I, is with a singular third person, and are with we or they.
Describe a routine
How often do you update the plan? I update it every morning before our meeting.
The plan is updated every morning.
I usually ___ the planning meeting.
attend
She update the plan every day.
She updates the plan every day.
Every morning signals a routine, so use the present simple.
Say what is happening
What are you working on this week? I am checking the new UX design.
The speaker is checking a design now.
I am ___ the new design.
checking
I checking the new design.
I am checking the new design.
Present continuous needs am, is, or are before the -ing form.
Routine versus today
Do you usually work alone? Usually, yes, but today I am working with the team.
Today is different from the usual routine.
Today she ___ working with the team.
is
She work with us today.
She is working with us today.
Use the continuous for an action happening now or a temporary situation.
Ask about progress
Is the team testing the prototype? Not yet. They are finalizing the designs.
Design work is still happening.
They are ___ the designs.
finalizing
They are finalize the designs.
They are finalizing the designs.
After are in the continuous, use the -ing form. Finalize designs is a natural collocation.
Give a short status
What does the team need today? It needs a decision, and we are preparing two options.
The team needs a decision.
My job ___ it.
needs
The team need to deciding.
The team needs to decide.
Needs agrees with the team; to is followed by the base verb decide.
Report yesterday's work
What did you finish yesterday? I finished the budget summary before lunch.
The summary was finished yesterday.
Yesterday I ___ the budget summary.
sent
Yesterday I finish the summary.
Yesterday I finished the summary.
Use past simple for a completed action. Send becomes sent; finish becomes finished.
Ask about a past decision
Did they approve the budget? No, they asked for more information.
The budget was not approved.
Did they ___ the budget?
approve
Did they approved the budget?
Did they approve the budget?
After did, use the base verb, even when the question refers to the past.
Use a specific article
Where is the report we discussed? The report is in the shared folder.
The report is in a shared folder.
Please open ___ report we discussed.
the
Please open report we discussed.
Please open the report we discussed.
Use the for a specific thing already identified by both speakers.
Choose a work preposition
What are you working on? I am working on the launch plan, but I am waiting for approval.
The speaker is waiting for approval.
I'm working ___ the launch plan.
on
I am working in the launch plan.
I am working on the launch plan.
Work on a task; wait for a person, decision, or event.
Tell a short past story
How did the review go? We found a problem, discussed two options, and chose a smaller scope.
The team chose a smaller scope.
We ___ a problem in the review.
found
We find a problem yesterday.
We found a problem yesterday.
Find becomes found in the past; choose becomes chose.
Explain a reason
Why is the release delayed? The release is delayed because we need another test.
Another test is the reason for the delay.
We need another test, ___ the release is delayed.
so
The release is delayed because of we need a test.
The release is delayed because we need a test.
Because introduces a clause; because of introduces a noun phrase.
Contrast two ideas
Is the design finished? The design is finished, but the budget is still under review.
The budget review is still open.
The design is ready, ___ the budget is not.
but
Although the design is ready, but we need approval.
Although the design is ready, we need approval.
Use although with a clause; do not add but to the same construction.
Explain a sequence
How do we start the review? First, read the summary. Next, check the risks. Finally, agree on an owner.
Reading the summary is the first step.
___, read the summary; next, check the risks.
First
First read the summary, finally check risks, next agree.
First read the summary, next check risks, finally agree.
First starts a sequence; next continues it; finally marks its last step.
Ask someone to repeat
Could you repeat that? Do you mean we should send the draft today or tomorrow? Tomorrow, please.
The draft should be sent tomorrow.
Could you ___ that, please?
repeat
Could you to repeat that?
Could you repeat that?
After could, use a base verb without to. Ask a focused follow-up after requesting repetition.
Clarify your meaning
Let me clarify. The prototype is ready for internal review, not for release.
The prototype is only ready for internal review.
What I ___ is that we can review it internally.
mean
Let me to clarify the next step.
Let me clarify the next step.
Let + person + base verb: let me clarify. Use What I mean is to repair a message.
Share completed and current work
What is your update? We finished the draft yesterday, and today we are checking the figures.
The figures are being checked today.
Today we are ___ the figures.
checking
We finished yesterday and today we checks figures.
We finished yesterday and today we are checking figures.
Switch tense when the time changes: finished yesterday; are checking today.
Describe a blocker
What is blocking the team? We cannot start testing because we are waiting for budget approval.
Budget approval is blocking testing.
We cannot start ___ without approval.
testing
We cannot start to testing.
We cannot start testing.
Start can take an -ing form or to + base verb, but never to testing.
Name a dependency
What does the launch depend on? It depends on the architecture review, which is scheduled for Thursday.
The launch depends on a architecture review.
The launch depends ___ the architecture review.
on
The launch depends of the review.
The launch depends on the review.
The fixed phrase is depend on, not depend of.
State the next step
What happens next? We need to finalize the designs before we can ask for approval.
The designs must be finalized first.
We need to ___ the designs.
finalize
We need to finalizing the designs.
We need to finalize the designs.
Need to takes a base verb. Before links the earlier action to the later one.
Close an open issue
Are you still working on the open issue? Yes, I am working on closing it before Friday.
The speaker aims to close the issue before Friday.
I am working on ___ the issue.
closing
I am working on close the issue.
I am working on closing the issue.
After the preposition on, use a noun or an -ing form.
Make a plan
What are you going to do next week? We are going to test the prototype with three volunteers.
Testing is planned for next week.
We are going ___ test the prototype.
to
We going to test next week.
We are going to test next week.
Going to needs a form of be: we are going to test.
Offer immediate help
Who can take notes? I will take them. Please start the discussion.
The speaker volunteers to take notes.
I ___ take the notes.
will
I will to take the notes.
I will take the notes.
Will takes a base verb without to; it can express a decision made now.
Confirm an arrangement
When are you meeting the designer? We are meeting her at ten tomorrow. It is already in the calendar.
The meeting is arranged for ten tomorrow.
We ___ meeting the designer tomorrow.
are
We meeting her at ten tomorrow.
We are meeting her at ten tomorrow.
Present continuous can describe an arranged future event with a clear time.
Give a realistic estimate
When do you expect to finish? We can finish the draft by Friday, but the final review will take another day.
Only the draft can be finished by Friday.
The review will ___ another day.
take
The review will takes another day.
The review will take another day.
After will, use take. Distinguish a draft deadline from a final approval deadline.
Explain a condition
Will we launch on Monday? If the review passes, we will launch on Monday. Otherwise, we will wait.
Monday's launch depends on the review.
If the review ___, we will launch.
passes
If the review will pass, we will launch.
If the review passes, we will launch.
In a first conditional, use present simple after if and will in the result clause.
Open a meeting
What should we cover first? First, let us confirm the goal. Then we can discuss the open risks.
The meeting starts by confirming the goal.
Let us ___ the goal first.
confirm
Let us to confirm the goal.
Let us confirm the goal.
Let us takes a base verb. An agenda tells people what comes first and next.
Ask a focused question
When does the review start? It starts at two, and the designer will lead it.
The review begins at two.
When ___ the review start?
does
When does the review starts?
When does the review start?
Use does + subject + base verb in a present-simple question.
Check understanding
I am not sure I understood. Are you asking for a new design or a small change? Just a small change.
Only a small change is requested.
I am not sure I ___.
understood
I am not sure I understanded.
I am not sure I understood.
The past form of understand is understood. Offer two interpretations to check meaning.
Interrupt politely
Sorry to jump in. Could we confirm who owns the next action before we move on?
The speaker wants to confirm an action owner.
Sorry ___ jump in.
to
Sorry for jump in.
Sorry to jump in.
Sorry to jump in is a useful polite interruption; sorry for is followed by an -ing form.
Summarize decisions
What did we agree? We agreed to reduce the scope and send the revised plan by Wednesday.
A revised plan is due Wednesday.
We agreed ___ reduce the scope.
to
We agreed reduce the scope.
We agreed to reduce the scope.
Agree to + verb describes a shared decision to act.
Request a missing input
What do you need from us? We need the final figures by noon so that we can send the report today.
Final figures are needed by noon.
We need the figures ___ noon.
by
We need the figures until noon.
We need the figures by noon.
By sets a deadline; until describes something continuing up to a time.
Explain an impact
What happens if the review is late? A late review will delay testing by two days.
Testing could be delayed by two days.
A late review will ___ testing.
delay
A late review will delays testing.
A late review will delay testing.
Will + base verb expresses a possible future impact. Quantify the impact when you can.
Escalate with context
Why are you escalating this? We asked for approval on Monday, and we still have no decision. Testing starts tomorrow.
A missing decision threatens tomorrow's testing.
We asked ___ approval on Monday.
for
We asked approval on Monday.
We asked for approval on Monday.
Ask for a thing; ask someone a question. Include the request history and the decision needed.
Compare two priorities
Which task comes first? Fix the sign-in issue first because it prevents people from testing. The new icon can wait.
The sign-in issue has higher priority.
The icon can ___ until tomorrow.
wait
The icon can waits until tomorrow.
The icon can wait until tomorrow.
Modal verbs such as can take the base verb. Prioritize by impact, not only effort.
Name a trade-off
Should we add the extra screen? It gives more detail; however, it adds two days of work. We need a decision today.
The extra screen adds detail and work.
The extra screen ___ two days of work.
adds
It give detail however it adds work.
It gives detail; however, it adds work.
However connects contrasting statements and is normally separated with punctuation.
Delegate a clear task
Could you review the summary by Thursday and flag any missing costs? Yes, I will send comments before lunch.
The task is a cost-focused review due Thursday.
Could you ___ the summary by Thursday?
review
Could you reviews the summary?
Could you review the summary?
A clear request names the action, scope, and deadline; could takes the base verb.
Give specific feedback
What should I change in the update? Keep the summary, but add an owner and a date for each risk.
Each risk needs an owner and a date.
Each risk ___ an owner.
needs
Each risk need an owner.
Each risk needs an owner.
Each takes a singular verb. Specific feedback tells the listener what to change.
Distinguish risk from issue
Is the supplier delay confirmed? No. It might happen next week, so we should prepare a backup plan.
The supplier delay is a possible future risk.
The delay might ___ next week.
happen
The delay might happens next week.
The delay might happen next week.
Might + base verb describes uncertainty. A risk is possible; an issue is already happening.
Propose mitigation
How can we reduce the risk? We can test a smaller sample now and keep one day for fixes.
Early sample testing is proposed to reduce risk.
We can reduce the risk ___ testing a sample.
by
We reduce the risk by test a sample.
We reduce the risk by testing a sample.
By + -ing explains the method used to achieve a result.
Balance two viewpoints
Why not release today? The team wants quick feedback. On the other hand, support needs time to prepare instructions.
A fast release conflicts with support preparation.
Support ___ time to prepare.
needs
Support need time to prepare.
Support needs time to prepare.
On the other hand introduces a competing perspective. Support as a department takes needs here.
Negotiate more time
Can you deliver tomorrow? We can send the draft tomorrow, but we need two more days for the checked version.
The checked version requires two more days.
We need two more days ___ the checked version.
for
We need two days more for checking version.
We need two more days for the checked version.
Two more days is natural word order; distinguish the draft from the checked deliverable.
Offer a smaller scope
Is Friday possible? Yes, if we remove the optional chart. We can add it in the next version.
Friday is possible with reduced scope.
If we ___ the chart, Friday is possible.
remove
If we will remove the chart, Friday is possible.
If we remove the chart, Friday is possible.
Present simple after if states the condition for a feasible agreement.
Disagree constructively
Do you agree with the new date? I see the benefit, but I am concerned about the testing time. Could we keep one extra day?
The speaker is concerned about testing time.
I am concerned ___ the testing time.
about
I am concerned for the testing time.
I am concerned about the testing time.
Concerned about introduces a worry. Acknowledge the benefit before stating a concern.
Confirm an agreement
What is the final agreement? We will deliver the core screens on Friday and the optional chart next Tuesday.
The optional chart is due next Tuesday.
We will ___ the core screens on Friday.
deliver
We will delivery the screens on Friday.
We will deliver the screens on Friday.
Deliver is a verb; delivery is a noun. Confirm scope and dates separately.
Handle a missed deadline
Why did we miss the date? We underestimated the review time. We have revised the plan and will share daily updates.
Review time was underestimated.
We ___ the review time.
underestimated
We did not estimated the review time well.
We did not estimate the review time well.
After did not, use a base verb. Explain what happened and the recovery action without blame.
Introduce your experience
Tell me about your role in Project Orion. I coordinated a small team and helped it turn goals into weekly plans.
The speaker coordinated planning.
I ___ a small team on Project Orion.
coordinated
I was coordinate a small team.
I coordinated a small team.
Use past simple for a completed role; was coordinated would be passive and change the meaning.
Describe a challenge
Tell me about a difficult situation. A review was late, so I proposed a smaller release and confirmed a new date.
The speaker responded to a late review with a smaller release.
I ___ a smaller release.
proposed
I proposed to a smaller release.
I proposed a smaller release.
Propose can take a noun directly: propose a plan or a smaller release.
Explain a result
What was the outcome? We delivered the core features on time. As a result, the team could collect feedback that week.
Timely delivery allowed feedback that week.
As a result, we ___ collect feedback.
could
As result we could collect feedback.
As a result, we could collect feedback.
As a result introduces an outcome; it includes the article a.
Keep small talk going
How was your weekend? It was relaxing. I went for a walk. How about yours?
The speaker went for a walk.
I ___ for a walk.
went
I goed for a walk.
I went for a walk.
Go has the irregular past went. Answer briefly and return a friendly question.
Ask about a new role
Do you have any questions for us? Yes. What would success look like in the first three months?
The candidate asks about early expectations.
What would success ___ like?
look
What would success looks like?
What would success look like?
Would takes a base verb. A focused interview question helps clarify expectations.
Give a three-part update
What is the latest? We fixed the issue yesterday. We are testing today. If the tests pass, we will release tomorrow.
Tomorrow's release depends on today's tests.
If the tests pass, we will ___ tomorrow.
release
Yesterday we fix it and tomorrow we released.
Yesterday we fixed it and tomorrow we will release.
Match tense to the time marker and keep a future condition explicit.
Explain a complex choice
Why choose the smaller option? It costs less and is easier to support. Although it has fewer features, it meets the main need.
The smaller option meets the main need with less cost.
Although it ___ fewer features, it meets the need.
has
Although it has fewer features, but it meets the need.
Although it has fewer features, it meets the need.
Although already signals contrast, so do not pair it with but in the same sentence.
Recover during a conversation
What does dependency mean here? It means we cannot start testing until the design is approved.
Testing must wait for design approval.
We cannot start testing ___ the design is approved.
until
What means dependency here?
What does dependency mean here?
For a present-simple question, use does + subject + mean. Until marks the required waiting point.
Lead a short decision
Which option should we choose? First, compare the risks. Then, choose an owner. Finally, confirm the deadline together.
The group should compare risks before selecting an owner.
Finally, ___ the deadline together.
confirm
We should to compare the risks.
We should compare the risks.
Should takes a base verb. A structured decision ends with a clear owner and deadline.
Reflect and plan forward
What will you keep practicing? I will practice asking clear questions and giving short updates. I can now explain a blocker more clearly.
The speaker plans to practice questions and updates.
I will practice ___ clear questions.
asking
I will practice to ask clear questions.
I will practice asking clear questions.
Practice takes an -ing form. Reflect on observable skills rather than claiming a guaranteed language level.

translations: ¿Qué haces en Project Orion? Coordino el equipo de diseño.
¿Quién revisa el informe semanal? La persona que coordina el proyecto lo revisa cada viernes.
¿La diseñadora asiste a la reunión de planificación? Sí, asiste cada lunes.
¿Qué necesitan para empezar? Primero necesitamos revisar el diseño.
¿Eres quien coordina el proyecto? Sí. Trabajo con dos diseñadores.
¿Con qué frecuencia actualizas el plan? Lo actualizo cada mañana antes de nuestra reunión.
¿En qué estás trabajando esta semana? Estoy revisando el nuevo diseño de UX.
¿Normalmente trabajas sin compañía? Generalmente sí, pero hoy estoy trabajando con el equipo.
¿El equipo está probando el prototipo? Todavía no. Está finalizando los diseños.
¿Qué necesita el equipo hoy? Necesita una decisión y estamos preparando dos opciones.
¿Qué terminaste ayer? Terminé el resumen del presupuesto antes del almuerzo.
¿Aprobaron el presupuesto? No, pidieron más información.
¿Dónde está el informe que discutimos? Está en la carpeta compartida.
¿En qué estás trabajando? Estoy trabajando en el plan de lanzamiento, pero estoy esperando la aprobación.
¿Cómo fue la revisión? Encontramos un problema, discutimos dos opciones y elegimos un alcance menor.
¿Por qué se retrasó el lanzamiento? Porque necesitamos otra prueba.
¿El diseño está terminado? Sí, pero el presupuesto sigue en revisión.
¿Cómo empezamos la revisión? Primero, lee el resumen. Después, revisa los riesgos. Finalmente, acuerda quién se hará cargo.
¿Podrías repetirlo? ¿Quieres decir que enviemos el borrador hoy o mañana? Mañana, por favor.
Déjame aclararlo. El prototipo está listo para revisión interna, no para su lanzamiento.
¿Cuál es tu avance? Terminamos el borrador ayer y hoy estamos revisando las cifras.
¿Qué está bloqueando al equipo? No podemos empezar las pruebas porque esperamos la aprobación del presupuesto.
¿De qué depende el lanzamiento? De la revisión de arquitectura, programada para el jueves.
¿Qué sigue? Necesitamos finalizar los diseños antes de pedir la aprobación.
¿Sigues trabajando en el asunto pendiente? Sí, estoy trabajando para cerrarlo antes del viernes.
¿Qué van a hacer la próxima semana? Vamos a probar el prototipo con tres voluntarios.
¿Quién puede tomar notas? Yo las tomaré. Por favor, empieza la discusión.
¿Cuándo te reunirás con la diseñadora? Nos reuniremos a las diez mañana. Ya está en el calendario.
¿Cuándo esperan terminar? Podemos terminar el borrador para el viernes, pero la revisión final tardará otro día.
¿Lanzaremos el lunes? Si la revisión pasa, sí. De lo contrario, esperaremos.
¿Qué debemos tratar primero? Primero confirmemos el objetivo. Después podremos discutir los riesgos pendientes.
¿A qué hora empieza la revisión? A las dos, y la diseñadora la dirigirá.
No estoy seguro de haber entendido. ¿Pides un diseño nuevo o un cambio pequeño? Solo un cambio pequeño.
Perdón por interrumpir. ¿Podemos confirmar quién es responsable de la siguiente acción antes de continuar?
¿Qué acordamos? Reducir el alcance y enviar el plan revisado para el miércoles.
¿Qué necesitan de nosotros? Las cifras finales para el mediodía para poder enviar el informe hoy.
¿Qué pasa si la revisión se retrasa? Retrasará las pruebas dos días.
